content: 1. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate regular strength tablets should be chewed, with a recommended dose of 2-4 tablets taken orally every 6 hours as needed. Do not exceed 16 tablets per day. The safety and efficacy of this regimen have not been established. 2. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of raltegravir by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The combination is contraindicated and not recommended, even with dose separation. 3. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces atazanavir solubility. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, administer atazanavir 2 hours before or 1 hour after the antacid. 4. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Baloxavir may bind to polyvalent cations, leading to decreased absorption. Animal studies have shown significant reductions in plasma levels when coadministered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. Human studies have not been conducted. 5. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and coadministration with drugs that increase gastric pH may cause premature dissolution, potentially affecting drug release and absorption in the duodenum. 6. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of cabotegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Administer antacid products at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after taking oral cabotegravir. 7. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that alter upper gastrointestinal tract pH, such as proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), H2-blockers, and antacids, may reduce dabrafenib solubility and bioavailability. 8. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration from antacids by at least 2 hours. 9. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate increases the levels of ethambutol by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid administering aluminum hydroxide-containing antacids for at least 4 hours following an ethambutol dose. 10. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Avoid this interaction by administering antacids 2 hours before or 2 hours after nilotinib. 11. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Separate the dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 12. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of pazopanib with drugs that raise gastric pH. Short-acting antacids may be used instead of PPIs and H2 antagonists, but antacid and pazopanib dosing should be separated by several hours. 13. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Separate pexidartinib administration by 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid. 14. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of rifampin by reducing its absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. Concomitant antacid administration may reduce rifampin absorption. Daily doses of rifampin should be given at least 1 hour before antacid ingestion. 16. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels of riociguat by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least 1 hour. 17. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Separate the dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 18. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases (practically insoluble at pH >5). Separate administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir from antacids by at least 4 hours. 19. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate reduces the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering its solubility and bioavailability due to increased gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. The effect on efficacy is unknown. 20. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate may cause hypersensitivity reactions, tinnitus, or hearing impairment, which could indicate toxicity. Use caution in patients with renal failure or those on magnesium-restricted diets. This medication may alter the absorption of concomitantly administered oral drugs by changing gastrointestinal transit time, pH, or through cationic binding. 21. Pregnancy Category C: The effects of aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate on pregnancy are not well established. Lactation: It is unknown whether this medication is distributed in breast milk. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
